Quick checks from finance: we can do split invoicing but with constraints — our billing engine only supports per-line invoice-to override when a PO is present and when the order lines are explicitly tagged as "Subscription" vs "Services". Operationally that means:

- Order form needs a mapping table: line item categories -> invoice entity (we can provide a one-line table in redline).
- For recurring subscription charges we can bill Horizon US monthly and route any one-time professional services to Horizon EU.
- Taxes: we will list taxes on the invoice if the customer provides a valid local VAT registration number and a written statement that Horizon will self-assess (reverse charge). Otherwise we will apply VAT where required.
- Net terms: standard Redwood is Net 30 for hosted subscriptions; we can accept Net 45 on enterprise deals with approvals. Net 60 is atypical — if Horizon needs Net 60 we should consider (a) an upfront partial prepay or (b) a short credit review and approval from finance.

I've attached a short doc with the recommended invoice-routing clause and a sample table you can paste into the order form. If Horizon insists on Net 60 without prepay, we should get finance sign-off and potentially price for the additional credit risk.
